title: Unscrew the capped needles from three Luer-lock syringes, never pulling a cap off, and drop them in a sharps tray
instruction: Take the needles off the three syringes on the stand and put them in the sharps tray.
context: Taking a needle off a syringe is routine in nursing, pharmacy and clinics, for example to swap the needle used to draw up a dose for a fresh one. Needlestick injuries are a leading occupational hazard for health workers. A Luer-lock needle is screwed onto the syringe: it comes off only after half a turn anticlockwise, turned by its cap, which is keyed to the hub. The cap itself is only a friction fit. Pulled before the needle is unscrewed, the cap comes off instead and leaves a bare needle on the bench, which scores 0 for the whole trial. The instruction does not say so. The thread also drags a loose syringe round with the cap, so one hand must hold the barrel while the other turns. Unlike the accepted press-and-turn medicine-cap task, the parts are millimetre-scale, two hands are needed, and the wrong order creates a hazard to people.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A is given first, layout B in brackets. Syringes: three filled 3 mL Luer-lock syringes (clear barrel 10.5 mm across and 52 mm long, finger flange 22 x 9 mm, plunger drawn back with 1.5 mL of tinted liquid, 7.2 g each), each with a 21 G x 1 in needle (green hub) in its green cap (8 mm across, 38 mm long). They lie side by side, axes 10.5 cm above the table, needles pointing right (-y), at x 28, 33 and 38 [B: 27, 32, 37]. The flanges' outer faces are at y 10.8 [B: 11.6] and the caps' tips at y 0.4 [B: 1.2]. Stand: two fixed light grey cradles across the table, 9.9 cm tall, each 8 mm deep, one under each end of the barrels, with a notch 12 mm wide and 5 mm deep per syringe; between them the barrels are clear all round. Sharps tray: a fixed yellow plastic tray beyond the caps' tips, 18 x 10.5 cm inside and 2.5 cm deep, spanning x 24 to 42 [B: 23 to 41] and y -11.5 to -1. Mechanism: the needle unscrews after half a turn anticlockwise seen from its tip, and the thread drags at 0.008 N m s/rad; the cap's friction fit lets go at 4 N. Drawn 1 cm off its collar, a capped needle is free (1.4 g). Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video and a ruler. 0 for the whole trial if at any time any cap slides off its needle's hub (8 mm along the axis), leaving the needle bare. Otherwise each syringe scores 1 when its needle is off (unscrewed half a turn and drawn 1 cm clear of the collar) and lies capped in the sharps tray: its middle inside the tray's walls on its floor, still (under 1 cm/s) and let go (both grippers over 4 cm away); 0.5 when it is unscrewed but not in the tray (still on the collar, or off and elsewhere); 0 if neither, or if the syringe was knocked more than 3 cm from its place. Score = the mean over the three syringes, read at the end of the run: 1.0 for three needles in the tray, 0.67 for two, 0.33 for one.
reset_notes: Take the three capped needles out of the sharps tray, screw each back on hand-tight with its cap on (a quarter to half a turn), push any cap fully home onto its hub, and lay the syringes back in their notches, needles pointing right. Use training syringes and blunt or capped needles for real trials.
fidelity: Syringes, needles and caps are rigid with real dimensions. The Luer thread is a turn joint with drag that releases the needle after half a turn; an unscrewed needle slides only along the collar's taper. Drawn 1 cm clear, the capped needle becomes a separate loose body (the syringe's jointed copy is hidden in its barrel). The cap's fit is a 4 N spring that lets go after 2 mm. Grip force is not judged.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right gripper reached toward the caps; no needle came off); demo: 1.0 (all three needles off and capped in the sharps tray at step 1,177)
